title: Leading a band for a UN deputy ambassador
summary: Hall got jobs through a deputy ambassador he met at Gregory's.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Right. And, I guess, daily you come into contact with -- with just all strata of society. Now, I know you did some things for Ambassador to the UN Scally.

Well, I was working with Al Slagans at Gregory's, and I met Robert Kitchen, who's deputy ambassador to the UN for the United States. He's in Morocco right now. And he used to come in every night and he got us for the job.

And I can't think of the names of the guys I had -- not right now I can't. But we had a good band. And I did a couple other things for him. One time he wanted two country fiddle players. And I had to scour and find two guys that hadn't played fiddle in years.
(Inaudible) Practicing in back seat of the car, banjo and fiddle. I thought I was going to get contractorship when Andrew Young became ambassador, but they don't believe in parties.
